prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The density-weight update rule (hpwl-based) uses a fixed multiplicative band [LOWER_PCOF, UPPER_PCOF] around a fixed reference HPWL; tightening the upper growth cap and making the growth factor more conservative when HPWL stops improving will keep density weight from overshooting, yielding more uniform cell spreading and thus more room for the fixed timing-repair pass to insert buffers on critical bottom-tier nets, reducing TNS.
Rule-based digest:
total=-inf robust(mean-std)=-inf min_case=-inf all_valid=False
  failures: bp_fe-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp_fe-ng45/1002:KeyError in partition; bp_fe-ng45/1003:stage timeout; bp-ng45/1001:stage timeout; bp-ng45/1002:HBT min-spacing violation; bp-ng45/1003:stage timeout
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Invalid: mixed timeout (4 runs, including all seeds of bp_fe-ng45/1001 and bp-ng45/1003), one crash (KeyError in partition, bp_fe-ng45/1002), and one legality failure (HBT min-spacing, bp-ng45/1002). Timeouts look systematic per-case; crash/legality sporadic. So the candidate says nothing about the hypothesis. To make it legal: profile and cap the density-weight loop's runtime, guard the partition KeyError, and add a spacing-repair/legality check after weight updates before timing repair.
